Description:
As an applicant, I want to enter my full name, date of birth, mobile number, email and residential address, so that I can apply for a savings account without visiting a branch.
Acceptance criteria:
1. Given I have started an application, when I reach the details step, then I can enter full name, date of birth, mobile number, email and residential address.
Notes: In scope on mobile and web (C s2). Field formats and validation [not stated].

As the bank, I want to accept only applicants aged 18 or over, so that the minimum-age rule is met.
Acceptance criteria:
1. Given I am under 18, when I apply, then I cannot open an account.
2. Given I am 18 or over, when I apply, then I am not stopped by the age rule.
Notes: Role 'the bank' is an assumption (no role named). Where age is checked (date of birth entry or ID) and the message shown [not stated].

Summary: S-03: Verify mobile number with OTP
Description:
As an applicant, I want to verify my mobile number with a one-time passcode, so that my number is confirmed.
Acceptance criteria:
1. Given I have entered my mobile number, when I enter the OTP correctly, then my number is verified.
2. Given an OTP was issued, when 5 minutes have passed, then the OTP is no longer valid.
3. Given I have entered incorrect OTPs, when I reach 3 attempts, then no further attempts are allowed.
Notes: What happens after 3 failed attempts, resend rules and OTP delivery channel [not stated].

As an applicant, I want a progress bar, so that I can see how far through the application I am.
Acceptance criteria:
1. Given I am in the application journey, when I move between steps, then a progress bar shows my progress.
Notes: Number and naming of steps [not stated].

Summary: S-05: Submit photo ID and selfie for Veridian check
Description:
As an applicant, I want to upload a photo ID and take a selfie, so that my identity is verified without a branch visit.
Acceptance criteria:
1. Given I am at the ID step, when I upload a photo ID and take a selfie, then they are submitted to Veridian for verification.
2. Given Veridian has processed my submission, then it returns pass, fail or refer.
Notes: Vendor integration owner: Engineering, Ananya Rao (C s5). Contract signed, sandbox live (A 00:52). What the applicant sees on fail [not stated]. Refer handling is blocked by C-02 (see S-14, S-16 to S-19). Veridian response times not yet measured in sandbox (F).

As an applicant, I want live feedback while I take my selfie, so that I can fix problems before submitting instead of failing at the end.
Acceptance criteria:
1. Given I am capturing my selfie, when a problem is detected, then I see feedback during capture, not only after submission.
2. Given the image is too dark, then I see a 'too dark' message.
3. Given the image is too blurry, then I see a 'too blurry' message.
4. Given the selfie is not close enough, then I see a 'move closer' message.
5. Given I am wearing glasses, then I see a 'remove glasses' message.
Notes: Message list is Sanjay Mehta's draft (E); final wording [not stated]. D lists 'face partly covered' as a common failure but the draft list covers glasses only. Detection method and thresholds [not stated]. Selfie rejection rate unknown (F).

Summary: S-07: Accept T&Cs and privacy notice before submitting
Description:
As a compliance officer, I want applicants to accept the T&Cs and privacy notice before they can submit, so that Compliance's pre-submission acceptance requirement is met.
Acceptance criteria:
1. Given I have not accepted both the T&Cs and the privacy notice, when I try to submit, then I cannot submit.
2. Given I have accepted both, when I submit, then submission is allowed.
Notes: Compliance calls it non-negotiable (B). Whether acceptance is recorded, document content/owner and which step counts as 'submit' [not stated].

As an applicant, I want to save my progress and resume later, so that I can come back instead of dropping off.
Acceptance criteria:
1. Given I am partway through the application, when I save my progress, then it is stored.
2. Given I saved progress, when I return within 14 days and log back in with a mobile OTP, then I can resume.
Notes: Behaviour after 14 days and whether S-03 OTP rules apply at login [not stated]. Retention of abandoned data is undecided (U-01).

Summary: S-09: Audit log of KYC decisions
Description:
As a compliance officer, I want every KYC decision logged, so that decisions can be audited.
Acceptance criteria:
1. Given a KYC decision of pass, fail or refer is made, then an audit log entry is created.
2. Given an audit log entry exists, then it is kept for 7 years.
Notes: Owner: Data Platform, Lena Ortiz (C s5). Entry contents, retrieval and access [not stated]. 'KYC decision' assumed to mean the Veridian outcome; whether manual review outcomes (S-15, S-16) are also logged [not stated].

Summary: S-10: Issue account number on approval
Description:
As an applicant, I want an account number issued when my application is approved, so that I can use my account.
Acceptance criteria:
1. Given my application is approved, then an account number is issued.
Notes: 'Approval' is not defined (G-03). Funding method TBD (C FR-7, U-02) although A 00:24 expects the account to be funded and usable.

Summary: S-11: SMS confirmation when account opened
Description:
As an applicant, I want an SMS when my account is opened, so that I know it is open.
Acceptance criteria:
1. Given my account has been opened, then an SMS is sent to my mobile number.
2. Given the SMS is sent, then it is sent through Textline.
Notes: Textline, same as the cards team, confirmed by Priya (E). Message text and language [not stated]. 'Account opened' see G-03.

As an applicant, I want an email with the welcome pack, so that I receive my welcome pack.
Acceptance criteria:
1. Given my account has been opened (assumed trigger), then an email with the welcome pack PDF is sent to the email address I entered.
2. Given the welcome pack is sent at launch, then it is in English.
Notes: Email trigger is not stated; assumed same as the SMS. Template owner: Design, Sanjay Mehta, half done (A 02:13; C s5). Email subject and body [not stated].

As an applicant, I want the onboarding service to be available, so that I can complete my application without interruption.
Acceptance criteria:
1. Given a month, when availability is measured, then it is at least 99.9%.
Notes: What is measured (which components, vendor dependency), exclusions such as planned maintenance, and the measurement method [not stated].

Summary: S-14: Straight-through processing with zero manual review
Description:
As an applicant, I want my application processed straight through without manual review, so that I can open my account on my phone in about five minutes.
Acceptance criteria:
1. Given I submit an application, when it is processed, then there is no manual review and ops do not touch it.
2. Given my ID is checked through Veridian, then the check is straight through.
Notes: BLOCKED by C-01 and C-02. Ananya's 'straight through' is scoped to the ID check via the vendor (A 00:41).

Summary: S-15: Manual Compliance review for addresses outside the country
Description:
As a compliance officer, I want applicants whose residential address is outside the country routed to manual Compliance review before activation, so that the regulator requirement is met.
Acceptance criteria:
1. Given an applicant's residential address is outside the country, when they submit, then the application is routed to manual Compliance review.
2. Given the Compliance review is not complete, then the account is not activated.
Notes: BLOCKED by C-01. Compliance: 'No exceptions', 'Not optional' (B); Priya disputes in B. Which country, how the address is judged to be outside it, and review outcomes [not stated].

Summary: S-16: Referral queue for Veridian 'refer' outcomes
Description:
As an ops rep, I want a queue of applications Veridian marks 'refer', so that I can work them.
Acceptance criteria:
1. Given Veridian returns 'refer' for an application, then it appears in the referral queue.
Notes: BLOCKED by C-02. Rep actions and outcomes, and who builds the queue [not stated].

Summary: S-17: Reason code on referred applications
Description:
As an ops rep, I want to see why an application was referred, so that I can work the case.
Acceptance criteria:
1. Given an application is in the referral queue, when I open it, then I can see its reason code.
Notes: BLOCKED by C-02. Reason code source and list [not stated].

Summary: S-18: Work referred cases within 1 business day
Description:
As an ops rep, I want referred cases worked within 1 business day, so that referred cases do not stall.
Acceptance criteria:
1. Given a case is marked referred, then it is worked within 1 business day.
Notes: BLOCKED by C-02. Source calls it a target. 'Working' (picked up or resolved) and the business-day calendar [not stated]. See G-06.

Summary: S-19: Dashboard of applications stuck in referred over 24h
Description:
As an ops rep (assumed), I want a dashboard of applications stuck in referred for more than 24 hours, so that I can follow them up.
Acceptance criteria:
1. Given applications have been in referred status for more than 24 hours, when I open the dashboard, then they are listed.
Notes: BLOCKED by C-02. Dashboard users, fields and alerts [not stated]. See G-06.
